Question
========

A box sits on a frictionless surface. A `r M1` newtons force pushes the box `r d1`. Simultaneously a `r M2` newtons force pushes the box `r d2`.

What is the net force?

##ANSWER1## newtons ##ANSWER2##


Answerlist
--------

`r al1`
`r al2`



Solution
========


These forces are perpendicular. You should use Pythagorean Theorem to find the magnitude of the resultant (net) force.

$$|F_{\mathrm{net}}| = \sqrt{(F_{1})^2+(F_2)^2}$$


$$|F_{\mathrm{net}}| = \sqrt{`r M1`^2+`r M2`^2}$$

$$|F_{\mathrm{net}}| = \sqrt{`r M1^2`+`r M2^2`}$$


$$|F_{\mathrm{net}}| = \sqrt{`r M1^2+M2^2`}$$


$$|F_{\mathrm{net}}| = `r sqrt(M1^2+M2^2)`$$

The original numbers had 3 significant digits, so it seems like that is a good place to round our result.


$$|F_{\mathrm{net}}| = `r sprintf("%.2f",sqrt(M1^2+M2^2))`$$

And since the two forces were in directions `r d1` and `r d2`, the resultant will be somewhere between the two, so `r dd`.

Remember, vectors have both MAGNITUDE and DIRECTION.
